statement: Weighted least squares (WLS) is a generalization of ordinary linear regression that minimizes the weighted sum of squared residuals: \hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}} = \operatorname{arg\,min}_{\boldsymbol{\beta}} \sum_{i=1}^n w_i \left|y_i - \sum_{j=1}^m X_{ij}\beta_j\right|^2 = \operatorname{arg\,min}_{\boldsymbol{\beta}} \left\|W^{1/2}(\mathbf{y} - X\boldsymbol{\beta})\right\|^2, where w_i = W_{ii} > 0 is the weight associated with the ith observation and W is the diagonal matrix of weights.

symbols.meaning: vector of observed or measured values of the dependent variable
weighted least squares parameter estimate vector minimizing the objective function
diagonal weight matrix with diagonal entries W_{ii} = w_i
weight of the ith observation, ideally equal to 1/\sigma_i^2
variance of the ith observation measurement error
residual of the ith data point, r_i(\boldsymbol{\beta}) = y_i - f(x_i, \boldsymbol{\beta})
weighted sum of squared residuals objective function, S = \sum_{i=1}^n W_{ii} r_i^2 = \mathbf{r}^{\textsf{T}} W \mathbf{r}
variance-covariance matrix of the parameter estimates
hat matrix mapping observations to fitted values, H = X(X^{\textsf{T}}WX)^{-1}X^{\textsf{T}}W

properties.why: Stationarity condition obtained by setting the gradient of the weighted sum of squared residuals with respect to the parameters to zero
Explicit closed-form solution for the parameter estimates when X^{\textsf{T}}WX is invertible

properties.property: \hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}} is the Best Linear Unbiased Estimator (BLUE) when W_{ii} = 1/\sigma_i^2
properties.why: Aitken's theorem showing that minimizing the weighted sum of squares with weights equal to reciprocal variances yields the BLUE for uncorrelated observations with unequal variances
Whitening transformation factoring the diagonal weight matrix via w_{ii} = \sqrt{W_{ii}} to map the problem into ordinary least squares form

properties.property: M^\beta = (X^{\textsf{T}}WX)^{-1}X^{\textsf{T}}WMW^{\textsf{T}}X(X^{\textsf{T}}W^{\textsf{T}}X)^{-1}, which simplifies to M^\beta = (X^{\textsf{T}}WX)^{-1} when W = M^{-1}
properties.why: Error propagation from the observation error covariance matrix M to the parameter estimates

properties.property: M^{\mathbf{r}} = (I - H)M(I - H)^{\textsf{T}} = (I - H)M (when W = M^{-1})
properties.why: Linear relation between the residual vector \hat{\mathbf{r}} = (I - H)\mathbf{y} and observations \mathbf{y} implies residuals are correlated even if observations are uncorrelated

properties.property: X^{\textsf{T}}W\hat{\mathbf{r}} = \mathbf{0}, implying \sum_{i=1}^n W_i \hat{r}_i = 0 when the model contains a constant term (X_{i1} = 1)
properties.why: Left-multiplying the residual expression \hat{\mathbf{r}} = \mathbf{y} - X\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}} by X^{\textsf{T}}W identically cancels

assumptions.assumption: Observational errors are uncorrelated (off-diagonal entries of the error covariance matrix are zero) when using a diagonal weight matrix W
assumptions.breaks_when: Observations are correlated, in which case a non-diagonal weight matrix equal to the inverse of the full variance-covariance matrix of observations (generalized least squares) must be used

assumptions.assumption: Weights are known positive constants equal to the reciprocal of measurement variances (w_i = 1/\sigma_i^2)
assumptions.breaks_when: Variances are unknown from external sources and must be estimated from data using feasible generalized least squares or iteratively reweighted least squares

assumptions.assumption: The matrix X^{\textsf{T}}WX is non-singular and invertible
assumptions.breaks_when: The design matrix X lacks full column rank (collinear regressors) or weights are zero/negative

failure_modes.signature: X^{\textsf{T}}WX is non-invertible and normal equations cannot be uniquely solved
failure_modes.cause: Rank deficiency or multicollinearity in the design matrix X

failure_modes.mode: Suboptimal or biased variance estimation due to misspecified weights
failure_modes.signature: Estimator loses the BLUE property and parameter covariance matrix M^\beta fails to simplify to (X^{\textsf{T}}WX)^{-1}
failure_modes.cause: Weights do not equal the reciprocal measurement variances W \ne M^{-1}

failure_modes.mode: Underestimated parameter uncertainty from systematic errors
failure_modes.signature: True parameter error exceeds standard confidence limits derived from random error propagation
failure_modes.cause: Presence of systematic errors in observations which cannot be quantified by random error propagation
